syntax: ORDER BY due_day ASC NULLS LAST, id ASC
summary: Keep missing values after known values in an ascending sort.
documentation: SQLite normally sorts NULL before non-NULL values in ascending order. NULLS LAST changes that placement without substituting a made-up value. A second ordering key gives deterministic results when dates tie or are missing.
inputs: jobs(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, due_day INTEGER), where a NULL due_day means unscheduled.
returns: id and due_day ordered by ascending known day, then unscheduled jobs; id breaks ties.
caution: NULL placement belongs to each ordering expression. Without a tie-breaker, equal sort values have no guaranteed relative order. Numeric day values here are relative offsets, not date strings.
scenarios: Put scheduled jobs before unscheduled work in a queue.
Show known delivery offsets first without inventing a far-future date.
Sort imported records while keeping missing due dates visible at the end.
title: Put unscheduled jobs last
problem: Select id and due_day from jobs. Order due_day ascending with NULLS LAST, then id ascending for equal day values including NULL.
hint: Specify NULLS LAST on the due_day ordering term, then append id.
goal: Use ORDER BY ... NULLS LAST or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
